scenes.heading: Error Basics & the error Interface
scenes.narration: Let's cover Error Basics and the error Interface, the value-based way Go handles failure instead of exceptions.

scenes.heading: Errors are just values
items: error is an interface with one method: Error() string
A nil error conventionally means success
scenes.narration: In Go, errors are ordinary values, not exceptions. The built-in error is an interface with a single method, Error returning a string. Any type that implements it is an error. By convention a nil error means success. Fallible functions return a result and an error as their last value, and the caller immediately checks if err is not nil. This makes every failure path visible right in the source.

scenes.heading: An error travels up the stack
steps: Maps it to HTTP 404 and logs the chain
scenes.narration: Watch a record-not-found error bubble up. The database layer returns the sentinel sql.ErrNoRows. The repository wraps it with fmt.Errorf and the percent-w verb, adding context but preserving the original. The service wraps it again. At the top, the handler calls errors.Is to walk the whole chain, recognizes the sentinel, maps it to an HTTP 404, and logs the full story: load profile, get user, no rows in result set.

scenes.heading: Wrap with %w, match with errors.Is
scenes.narration: Here's the pattern in code. ErrNotFound is a sentinel error, a predeclared value. The get function wraps it with fmt.Errorf and the percent-w verb, which keeps the original inside the new error. Printing shows the combined message, get user, not found. And crucially, errors.Is walks the wrap chain and returns true, so a caller still recognizes the underlying cause even though the error was wrapped with extra context.

scenes.text: == only matches the exact error. Use errors.Is through a wrap chain, and errors.As to extract a type.
scenes.narration: A common mistake: comparing a wrapped error with double-equals fails, because the wrapper is a new value, not the sentinel itself. Always use errors.Is to match through the chain, and errors.As to pull out a concrete error type so you can read its fields. And reserve panic and recover for truly exceptional faults, not ordinary failures.
